_provenance.description: Cross-framework results for the crowd-sourced annotation (Dawid-Skene, marginalized) model under the STANDARD PPLBench protocol. NumPyro was added 2026-07-10; Impulse and Stan rows are reused verbatim from the G4 run (paper_data_G4_2026-07-06_052754.json / g4_results_G4_2026-07-06_052754.json).
_provenance.config: pplbench_configs/standard/crowd_sourced_annotation.json (model seed 12345, n=2000 -> 1000 train items, k=10, num_categories=3, expected_correctness=0.8, num_labels_per_item=3, concentration=10; iterations=4000, num_warmup=1000, trials=4, single chain per trial)
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains: overall n_eff = arviz.ess (min/median/max over all 62 params, 4 trials as 4 chains); n_eff/s = overall n_eff / mean steady-state (trials 1..3) inference wall time; PLL = per-trial final cumulative predictive log-likelihood on the held-out 1000 test items.

numpyro_run.env: conda probprog-bench python (numpyro 0.19.0, jax 0.9.0), matching how the other standard-model NumPyro bars were produced by run_pplbench.sh; NOT the local probprog/jax+numpyro tree (different jax version) so the bar is comparable to the other baselines.
numpyro_run.model_impl: pplbench/pplbench/ppls/numpyro/crowd_sourced_annotation.py (marginalized Dawid-Skene; analytic logsumexp over the discrete true label, matching the Stan and Impulse references)

Turing.jl.note: No marginalized Dawid-Skene Turing model exists in the tree (pplbench/pplbench/ppls/turing/ has no crowd_sourced_annotation.py). Turing does not auto-marginalize discrete latents, so a comparable arm would require a hand-written marginalized model; not created per task scope.
